This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products prepared in accordance with Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul (RFO) Part 12. The Government�s market research indicates that Agilent products use proprietary MassHunter software for instrument control and data analysis, and no other manufacturer produces a compatible system that meets the Government�s essential need for a single, integrated platform while avoiding the cost of new training and method redevelopment. title: Pakistan NDC 3.0 Delivery Coordination Mechanism (Federal-Provincial Coordination and Tracking)
description: The UK Government's Partnering for Accelerated Climate Transitions (UK PACT) programme is inviting proposals from qualified suppliers or consortia to deliver technical assistance to the Government of Pakistan. Pakistan has committed to reducing projected greenhouse gas emissions by 50% by 2035 through its Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) 3.0. Delivering this target will depend heavily on action at the provincial level, where responsibility for many climate-relevant sectors rests. While the Government of Pakistan has established new coordination arrangements through the National Climate Finance Strategy (NCFS), challenges remain around federal-provincial coordination, implementation tracking, climate finance visibility, and reporting progress against national climate commitments. The assignment will provide targeted technical assistance to support the Ministry of Climate Change and Environmental Coordination (MoCC&EC), the Pakistan Climate Change Authority (PCCA), and provincial governments to establish and operationalise a practical federal-provincial coordination and tracking mechanism for NDC 3.0 implementation. The project will strengthen institutional coordination, improve monitoring and reporting of climate actions and investments, build government capacity, and support the mobilisation of climate finance. The intervention will also integrate Gender Equality, Disability and Social Inclusion (GEDSI) considerations to promote more inclusive climate governance and decision-making. Key outputs are expected to include a federal-provincial NDC coordination framework, a standardised NDC tracking and reporting framework, an interoperability pilot connecting existing government climate and public-sector data systems, operational support for a Tactical Climate Coordination Forum, and a sustainability and scale-up roadmap. The project aims to strengthen Pakistan's ability to implement and report on its climate commitments, improve evidence-based decision-making, enhance transparency and accountability, and create a stronger foundation for attracting climate finance and accelerating NDC delivery across provinces and sectors. Interested suppliers are invited to review the documentation provided in this notice, and submit their applications to: targetedfund@ukpact.co.uk.

Historically, FOH has sourced MVMS from multiple vendors, including the Program Support Center�s fulfillment center. title: Barracks Maintenance OTA
description: 1. INTRODUCTION & SYNOPSIS This announcement is a formal Request for Prototype Proposal (RPP) issued by the Mission & Installation Contracting Command (MICC) � Fort Campbell on behalf of the Directorate of Public Works (DPW) at Fort Campbell, Kentucky. The Government is seeking competitive prototype proposals to design, integrate, and execute a modernized facility management solution across 58 unaccompanied housing (barracks) facilities. The prototype will integrate an advanced, secure Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) software platform with cross-trained physical maintenance execution to streamline work order triage, optimize Between Occupancy Maintenance (BOM), and execute proactive Preventative Maintenance Orders (PMO). Authority: 10 U.S.C. � 4022, Other Transaction Authority (OTA) for Prototype Projects. Agreement Type: The Government intends to award a single Other Transaction (OT) agreement. Follow-on Production / Sustainment: Offerors are advised that in accordance with 10 U.S.C. � 4022(f), successful completion of this prototype project may result in the award of a non-competitive, follow-on production/sustainment agreement or contract without further competition. 2. BACKGROUND Fort Campbell DPW is responsible for maintaining unaccompanied housing infrastructure that directly impacts Soldier readiness and Quality of Life (QoL). The current operating model relies heavily on manual administrative workflows, disparate tracking mechanisms, and reactive maintenance practices, leading to extended vacancy timelines during unit rotations, misdiagnosed service dispatches, and increased facility wear. This prototype project seeks to validate a modernized operational model that combines commercial best practices with enterprise Army platforms (including integration with ArMA, GFEBS, and the forthcoming enterprise IBM Maximo migration). Key modernization elements include QR-code-enabled request intake, automated work order routing, decentralized parts staging solutions (e.g., smart lockers), and dual-track maintenance (physical inspections for legacy systems and sensor-based monitoring for modern equipment). 3. ELIGIBILITY This RPP is open to all responsible business entities. In accordance with 10 U.S.C. � 4022(d)(1), an award may only be made if at least one of the following conditions is met: At least one nontraditional defense contractor or small business participates to a significant extent in the prototype project; OR All significant participants in the transaction other than the Federal Government are small businesses or nontraditional defense contractors; OR At least one-third (1/3) of the total cost of the prototype project is to be paid out of funds provided by sources other than the Federal Government (cost share); OR The Senior Procurement Executive provides written approval for exceptional circumstances. 4. PROPOSAL SUBMISSION & KEY DATES Proposal Instructions: Interested Offerors shall submit a comprehensive proposal package consisting of: Technical Approach (addressing EAM integration, physical maintenance, and predictive monitoring) Integrated Logistics & Sustainability Plan (addressing supply chain, SOPs, and knowledge transfer) Management, Programmatic, & Lifecycle Approach (Integrated Master Schedule, risk management, and scaling) Cost / Price Proposal Performance Work Statement (PWS) (directly derived from Attachment 001, Statement of Objectives) Key Dates: Questions Due Date: Sep 16, 2026, at 11:00 AM Central Time (CT) Site Visit Date: Sep 17, 2026, at 10:00 AM CT Proposal Due Date: Sep 25, 2026, at 11:00 AM Central Time (CT) Submission Instructions: Method: All questions and proposals must be submitted electronically via email. Email Address: evan.m.rea.civ@army.mil 5. GOVERNMENT POINTS OF CONTACT (POCs) Agreements Officer (AO): Eric C. Boston (eric.c.boston.civ@army.mil) Agreements Specialist / Contract Specialist: Evan M. title: Precision Inertial Navigation & Positioning On an Integrated Tesseract (PINPOINT)
description: The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) is soliciting innovative proposals in the following technical area: physics and nonlinear control of inertial measurement units (IMUs) appropriate for tactical and unmanned missions. The Precision Inertial Navigation & Positioning On an Integrated Tesseract (PINPOINT) program will challenge the research community to overcome the decade-long performance plateau of micro-electro-mechanical systems (MEMS) IMUs by exploring revolutionary sensor architectures that operate in highly nonlinear regimes. DARPA is soliciting proposals for the research and development of novel inertial sensors based on physics such as, but not limited to, electromagnetically levitated proof masses, non-linear resonators, and high-velocity tethered microsystems. A central theme of this program is the tight co-design of the physical sensor package with advanced, real-time adaptive control systems necessary to stabilize and harness these complex dynamics. Performers should investigate innovative approaches that enable revolutionary advances in science, devices, or systems. Specifically excluded is research that primarily results in evolutionary improvements to the existing state of practice.

title: Barracks Maintenance OTA
description: 1. INTRODUCTION & SYNOPSIS This announcement is a formal Request for Prototype Proposal (RPP) issued by the Mission & Installation Contracting Command (MICC) � Fort Campbell on behalf of the Directorate of Public Works (DPW) at Fort Campbell, Kentucky. The Government is seeking competitive prototype proposals to design, integrate, and execute a modernized facility management solution across 58 unaccompanied housing (barracks) facilities. The prototype will integrate an advanced, secure Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) software platform with cross-trained physical maintenance execution to streamline work order triage, optimize Between Occupancy Maintenance (BOM), and execute proactive Preventative Maintenance Orders (PMO). Authority: 10 U.S.C. � 4022, Other Transaction Authority (OTA) for Prototype Projects. Agreement Type: The Government intends to award a single Other Transaction (OT) agreement. Follow-on Production / Sustainment: Offerors are advised that in accordance with 10 U.S.C. � 4022(f), successful completion of this prototype project may result in the award of a non-competitive, follow-on production/sustainment agreement or contract without further competition. 2. BACKGROUND Fort Campbell DPW is responsible for maintaining unaccompanied housing infrastructure that directly impacts Soldier readiness and Quality of Life (QoL). The current operating model relies heavily on manual administrative workflows, disparate tracking mechanisms, and reactive maintenance practices, leading to extended vacancy timelines during unit rotations, misdiagnosed service dispatches, and increased facility wear. This prototype project seeks to validate a modernized operational model that combines commercial best practices with enterprise Army platforms (including integration with ArMA, GFEBS, and the forthcoming enterprise IBM Maximo migration). Key modernization elements include QR-code-enabled request intake, automated work order routing, decentralized parts staging solutions (e.g., smart lockers), and dual-track maintenance (physical inspections for legacy systems and sensor-based monitoring for modern equipment). 3. ELIGIBILITY This RPP is open to all responsible business entities. In accordance with 10 U.S.C. � 4022(d)(1), an award may only be made if at least one of the following conditions is met: At least one nontraditional defense contractor or small business participates to a significant extent in the prototype project; OR All significant participants in the transaction other than the Federal Government are small businesses or nontraditional defense contractors; OR At least one-third (1/3) of the total cost of the prototype project is to be paid out of funds provided by sources other than the Federal Government (cost share); OR The Senior Procurement Executive provides written approval for exceptional circumstances. 4. PROPOSAL SUBMISSION & KEY DATES Proposal Instructions: Interested Offerors shall submit a comprehensive proposal package consisting of: Technical Approach (addressing EAM integration, physical maintenance, and predictive monitoring) Integrated Logistics & Sustainability Plan (addressing supply chain, SOPs, and knowledge transfer) Management, Programmatic, & Lifecycle Approach (Integrated Master Schedule, risk management, and scaling) Cost / Price Proposal Performance Work Statement (PWS) (directly derived from Attachment 001, Statement of Objectives) Key Dates: Questions Due Date: Sep 16, 2026, at 11:00 AM Central Time (CT) Site Visit Date: Sep 17, 2026, at 10:00 AM CT Proposal Due Date: Sep 25, 2026, at 11:00 AM Central Time (CT) Submission Instructions: Method: All questions and proposals must be submitted electronically via email. Email Address: evan.m.rea.civ@army.mil 5. GOVERNMENT POINTS OF CONTACT (POCs) Agreements Officer (AO): Eric C. Boston (eric.c.boston.civ@army.mil) Agreements Specialist / Contract Specialist: Evan M. title: Measurement of Benzene Emissions from Gasoline Dispensing Facilities
description: Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC)’s mandate includes the preservation and enhancement of the quality of the natural environment, including water, air and soil quality. Accordingly, ECCC works in conjunction with Health Canada (HC) and other departments to understand the risks posed by the release of toxic substances, then develop policy as needed to effectively manage these releases. Benzene is recognized as a human carcinogen by HC (Canada 1993) and the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) (IARC 2018), among other international agencies. In addition, short-term exposure (over hours to days) is associated with hematotoxicity, including during fetal development. Benzene is a constituent of gasoline and, as a volatile organic compound (VOC), readily evaporates and is released into the atmosphere from gasoline service stations. Exposure to benzene through inhalation of emissions from these facilities may pose unacceptable risks to human health for members of the general population residing in the vicinity of gasoline stations. ECCC wishes to study benzene concentrations in the air in the vicinity of gasoline stations Canada, ideally in the Ottawa-Gatineau area, to improve understanding of the human health implications of benzene emissions from these facilities and validate the efficacy of emissions control equipment in cases where it is installed. The contractor will contribute to this objective by measuring ambient concentrations of benzene and, where feasible, other VOCs or total VOCs at gasoline stations before, during, and after gasoline deliveries, in accordance with the parameters set out in this Statement of Work. The Contractor must perform and complete the Work within the period commencing upon notification of acceptance of the offer and ending no later than March 31, 2027. For additional information, interested suppliers should contact Helena Lee at; Helena.Lee@ec.gc.ca.

Τα Check-up αποτελούν εξατομικευμένες τεχνικές εκθέσεις, διαφορετικές μεταξύ τους, οι οποίες απαιτούν ιδιαίτερη προσοχή ως προς την απόδοση της εξειδικευμένης ορολογίας και τη διατήρηση της δομής και του περιεχομένου κάθε αναφοράς. | Μετάφραση του ενιαίου παραδοτέου Business Re-engineering and Internationalisation Adaptation Plan (WP3). title: Service Integration and Management System (SIAM)
description: PSD Scotland intends to procure a Service Integration and Management contract for the transition, stabilisation and continued delivery of selected national digital services supporting health and care across Scotland. The successful supplier will act as prime contractor and provide a single point of accountability for end-to-end service delivery, integration and performance. The supplier will also be responsible for the management of any subcontractors and dependencies with other providers and Authority teams. The initial priority will be to maintain continuity and stabilise these business-critical services as they transition away from the existing National IT Contract, while establishing a strong foundation for subsequent improvement and modernisation.

title: Flood Bank Realignment
description: This collaborative project with SBAG address recurring concerns over beaver burrowing and floodbank breaches on high-value farmland along the River Isla, a major tributary of the River Tay (SAC). By realigning a floodbank and creating a wider more natural river corridor with willow buffer strip we intend to increase bank resilience, reduce beaver impacts and enhance biodiversity. Two participating agricultural landowners will trial setback embankments and habitat features including beaver mounds to encourage coexistence. The approach integrates agricultural resilience with river naturalisation, monitored by the river Restoration Centre and Beaver Trust to inform future coexistence strategies to promote biodiversity.

title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source USAGM Broadcasting/Transmission, Technical, Admin and O&M Services in Djibouti
description: THIS IS A NOTICE OF INTENT. This notice is issued in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) section 5.201 to notify the public of a proposed contract action. The North American Identification Classification System (NAICS) code is 516110 � Radio Broadcasting Stations. The SBA size standard is $47 million. The proposed contract action is for USAGM Broadcasting Operations and Maintenance in Djibouti. The U.S Agency of Global Media (USAGM) intends to award a contract, on a sole source basis under the authority of FAR 6.302-1, with Radiodiffusion Television de Djibouti (RTD). Radiodiffusion Television de Djibouti (RTD) Ave Street Laurent du Var Djibouti City, Djibouti The statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition is 41 U.S.C.3304(a)(1) as implemented by the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Subpart 6.302-1, which reads in part, �Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements.� Radiodiffusion Television de Djibouti is the only known source able to provide the required services. This requirement is for contractor support to reinstate, operate and maintain the radio transmitting facilities intended for the transmission of U.S. Government funded radio programs in Djibouti. ( See attached statement of work for requirement details) The Period of Performance will be a one year- Date of award plus 12 months. THIS NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE QUOTES. A determination by the Government not to compete this procurement based on responses to this notice is solely at the discretion of the Government. Interested parties who believe they possess the capability to satisfy this requirement should submit documentation that clearly demonstrates their capability. Responses to this notice shall be received no later than September 25, 2026 at 1:00PM EST. All responses must be in writing only via email to the point of contacts specified in this notice. Telephone requests or inquires will not be accepted. Any cost associated with the preparation and submission of data or information in response to this notice is the sole responsibility of the respondent and will not be reimbursed by the Government.

Past Experience � Include any prior experience with providing cafeteria services in a government or similar facility. Similar is defined as an office building with 100 or more employees including a hospital, military base, etc. Signed Solicitation, Offer and Award form (697DCK-26-R-00358) including completion of the Contractor Staffing Questionnaire, and signed amendments issued. An agreement will be made to the offeror that provides menu choices suitable and preferred by the facility. All proposals must reference the solicitation number (697DCK-26-R-00358) and be emailed to Noah.F.Laduca@faa.gov; jennifer.j.davis@faa.gov. Faxed or hard copy proposals will not be accepted. Proposals are due no later than 12 noon CT on Thursday, September 10, 2026. Contractors must have an Active SAM registration with the System for Award Management, www.sam.gov, on the date established for receipt of offers (September 10, 2026). The Government will not be liable for costs associated with the preparation and submittal of inquiries or responses to this announcement and will not reimburse any firm for costs incurred in responding to this SIR. Responses will not be returned. title: Access to Food and Cosmetic Product and Packaging Databases
description: The scope of this contract is to acquire the full range of technical, management and support services necessary to obtain and maintain access to US food and cosmetic products. The contract is divided into the following task areas: Project Management Data Access Data Collection Training Support 6.1 Technical Requirements 6.1.1 Datasets The processed food and cosmetic products and their package data (as well as menu data) shall be from a currently existing, commercially available database(s) that shall provide immediate automated access. The data shall include products from all regions of the US (Appendix B indicates the US Census regions) and be accurate, quality-assured, and easily-validated; well organized; stored as relationally searchable information for trend and other analyses; and fully exportable. The database(s) shall be regularly updated and maintained in a current state throughout the base and option periods. Information will be required for the following product types: Processed, and retail food products (e.g. foods, infant formula, etc.; minimum 400,000 products that are selling on the market in the contract year) and thus, over 2 million historical products; (Optional) Restaurant food products/menu items (minimum 50,000 products from top chains) Dietary supplements (minimum 100,000 products); shall be categorized according to the definition in Appendix A Cosmetics (minimum 300,000 products) The following attributes (as shown on the package) shall be required: Package images (legible images of all surfaces (e.g. sides, top, bottom) of product packaging, including internal and external packaging Count of available images per product Information contained on and in product packaging � shall include the following at minimum (each data entry line in the database must be quality assured and -controlled (QA/QC�d) for accuracy as the database is populated) GTIN/UPC/Barcode Nutrition Facts label, including single and dual columns and including multi-packs (shall be displayed in format according to 21 CFR 101.9) and Supplement Facts label (shall be displayed in format according to 21 CFR 101.36(e)(10) (i), (ii), (iii), and (iv)) Additional nutrients presenting on package labels Indication of added sugars Ingredients list (e.g. food additives, active ingredients for dietary supplements) Allergen labeling information (Contains/may contain) and advisory statements Pack size and weight Number of servings per package Brand Manufacturer Location of manufacturer, packer, or distributor Written and/or pictorial statements signaling the presence of one or more allergens (according to the Food Allergen Labeling and Consumer Protection Act (FALCPA) of 2004; e.g. �Contains�) and/or caution statements about the product (e.g. �warning statements�) Insignificant amounts for certain nutrients Claims on package (e.g., regulated, health, nutrition, efficacy, marketing, and all other types) including indication of �healthy� on package Statements/icons/signages and similar information that features the nutrition, health, organoleptic, processing, suggested usages (e.g., recipes), and other properties of the product (e.g., written and/or pictorial statements that feature nutrient content claim languages, front-of-pack language/icons) Certifications on package GE/Bioengineered/GMO language on package Verbatim language of all text (e.g. product description, instructions, etc.) and icons from product packaging Product source where collected Product category Dates of when product information is a) released to the market and on shelf, b) collected, c) published, d) updated, and e) discontinued Indication of �previous� or �new� nutrition facts label FNDDS 8-digit and 7-digit food codes; SR 5-digit sub codes (8-digit food code shall be linked to food products and ingredients;7-digit food codes are mapped to 8-digit at the product level; 5-digit SR sub codes are mapped to 8-digit food codes at the ingredient level) through 2019 GSFA (General Standard for Food Additives) categories through 2019 Food packaging types (primary and secondary) and codes Food content type Moreover, the data shall provide additional valid and verifiable information on the product ingredients; at a minimum, the data shall provide all available synonym name(s), allergen status, and technical or functional effect descriptors in a usable format. Additionally, FDA shall have access to other Mintel products, such as Mintel Leap, Mintel Food & Drink, Mintel Reports, Mintel Trends, Comperemedia Direct, Market Dynamics, and Global Consumer Research. 6.1.2 Product Requirements Overarching product requirements: Unlimited access for up to 200 FDA personnel; Located external to FDA network (access via weblink); Universal access from any FDA computer hardware (desktops, laptops with docking stations and/or scientific workstations) using internet browsers compatible with FDA current standards; Product access shall not be restricted according to product price; Capability to perform relational searching and analyses of the food and cosmetic product labeling and packaging datasets and menu datasets in functional environments using appropriate methodologies, which shall be valid, reliable, and robust; Ability to support disclosure of scientific and technical articles, study results, presentations, public health advisories, and similar works involving aggregated data to entities outside the Agency including the general public; High resolution, readable images for all sides of the package labels (and optionally, menu images) for validation and other research purposes. Images shall be displayed with product data from all sides of the package so that information may be easily verifiable by the user. Accurate data reflective of verbatim language and icons of product labels (and menus). Verification that products are still being sold in the US marketplace. Users shall be able to analyze and summarize their searches into summary reports and all available data and search results and outputs shall be downloadable and exportable within an accepted timeframe into Microsoft Excel Spreadsheets and Access Data Base Software, SAS Business Analytics Software, and other common formats. Regular, updated, extracted bulk/batch raw data of the full dataset shall be available by API and in MS Excel compatible format (e.g. single pipe delimited txt, csv) and shall be accessible in a secure FTP or cloud service acceptable by FDA. In addition to the product label (and menu) database(s), all sales data, other accompanying databases, and market research reports, when available, shall be provided. This information shall apply to food, dietary supplement, restaurant, and cosmetic products when available Data and UI status updates shall be posted on the system website main page and identified users shall be notified via email System usage statistics (including statistics regarding individual login usage and length of time logged in) shall be available in monthly reports and upon request All data and files shall undergo quality control checks prior to accessibility/delivery to FDA. Documentation on quality control procedures shall be provided (at the onset and with any changes over time) for all data and image collection and data processes (e.g. ingestion of data, quality assurance of data in different formats, etc.) as noted below. Web Interface A user-friendly and data comprehensive interface that is transparent and flexible and allows both predefined (i.e., canned) and custom reports shall be provided. The user should be able to conduct a multi-variable search (i.e. searching a combination of factors concurrently). The user should be able to search and filter according to product category, year, product name, UPC, brand, company, claims, ingredients, allergens, other product attributes, and user-entered keywords in any and all fields. title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source Collaborative Assessment and Management of Suicidality (CAMS) Training and Consultation for Tripler Army Medical Center (TAMC)
description: Notice of Intent to Sole Source HT941026N0127 THIS IS A NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE SOURCE SERVICE CONTRACT AND IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE QUOTES. The Defense Health Agency Contracting Activity (DHACA), Healthcare Contracting Division � West (HCD-W), San Diego, intends to negotiate and award a firm fixed price Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) for Collaborative Assessment and Management of Suicidality (CAMS) Training and Consultation Services in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul (RFO) 12.102(b) for purchases valued over the simplified acquisition threshold, only one source reasonably available to: CAMS-care, LLC 5712 Kingswood RD Bethesda, Maryland 20814 The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 611430 - Professional and Management Development Training the business size standard is $15.0M. The Product Service Code (PSC) is U009 - Education/Training � Other. The objective of this sole source award is to procure Collaborative Assessment and Management of Suicidality (CAMS) Training and Consultation Services for Tripler Army Medical Center (TAMC). CAMS-care, LLC is the sole proprietor, copyright owner, and intellectual property holder of the Collaborative Assessment and Management of Suicidality (CAMS) Framework�, the Suicide Status Form (SSF�), and the associated CAMS-Brief Intervention (CAMS-BI�) curricula. CAMS-care, LLC, holds exclusive copyrights, trademarks, and service marks for the CAMS multi-purpose clinical assessment and treatment framework. CAMS-care, LLC does not license third-party commercial training entities to deliver CAMS Foundation certification, CAMS-BI� role-play workshops, or official Suicide Status Form (SSF) chart-adherence fidelity evaluations. Consequently, CAMS-care, LLC is the sole entity legally authorized and operationally capable of providing the required training, curriculum licensing, fidelity audits, and certified internal trainer credentials. The specific proprietary attributes of the CAMS model are required to more effectively address suicide risk across its entire military healthcare delivery spectrum: Demonstrated Efficacy in Active-Duty Military Populations: The CAMS Framework� is an evidence-based clinical intervention supported by extensive randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and non-randomized clinical trials conducted directly with active-duty U.S. Army soldiers, military veterans, and civilian populations. The research literature validates that CAMS significantly reduces suicidal ideation, overall psychiatric symptom distress, and feelings of hopelessness while enhancing treatment retention and hope. Care Spectrum Versatility: The CAMS framework possesses unique adaptability across varying clinical acuities within military treatment facilities (MTFs): CAMS Standard Treatment: Designed for outpatient clinics, intensive outpatient programs (IOP), and partial hospitalization programs (PHP) spanning 6 to 12 longitudinal sessions until suicidal resolution is achieved. CAMS-Brief Intervention (CAMS-BI�): Structured for acute medical and psychiatric crisis settings (e.g., Emergency Departments, Inpatient Psychiatric Units, and Boarding Clinics) over 1 to 3 targeted sessions. Proprietary Core Instrument: CAMS centers on the Suicide Status Form (SSF), a collaborative clinical assessment, treatment planning, and tracking tool. The clinical algorithms, driver-identification methodologies, and ongoing tracking protocols within the SSF are proprietary. No commercial equivalent or alternate therapeutic model replicates the collaborative clinician-patient dynamic established by the SSF. The Government does not possess, nor does it have the legal data rights to acquire, the proprietary source code, copyrighted pedagogical courseware, or trademarked instructional guides underlying the CAMS training system. This procurement requires proprietary intellectual property, copyrighted clinical frameworks, and specialized training/certification methodologies that are exclusively owned, developed, and distributed by CAMS-care, LLC. No other commercial source satisfies the clinical, methodological, and operational requirements of the required activity. Period of Performance: 5-Year Ordering Period from 30 September 2026 to 29 September 2031. Place of Performance: Tripler Army Medical Center Department of Mental Health 1 Jarrett White Road Tripler Army Medical Center, HI 96859 Based on market research, CAMS-care, LLC is the only source that can meet the Government�s minimum requirements for the CAMS training and consultation services. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals, and no solicitation document exists for this requirement. Sources interested in responding to this notice are required to submit a capability statement that includes management and technical data and cost information, in sufficient detail and convincing evidence that clearly demonstrates the capability to provide the required services to TAMC. Capability statements shall not exceed six (8.5 x 11 inch) pages using a font size no smaller than 10-point. All capability statements received by the due date of this notice will be considered by the Government. A request for documentation or additional information or submissions that only ask questions will not be considered as an affirmative response. A determination by the Government not to compete based on responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement or to proceed with a sole source purchase order. If a vendor challenges the basis of this requirement, please email capability statements as a Microsoft Word or Adobe PDF attachment to April L. Delmendo at april.l.delmendo.civ@health.mil. The closing date for challenges is no later than 10:00am Pacific Time, 25 September 2026.

description: NAVSUP Fleet Logistics Center San Diego is seeking capable sources and industry input to provide Commander, Naval Surface Force, U.S. Pacific Fleet (CNSP) with Public Affairs and Visual Information (PA/VI) support services in San Diego, California via a SeaPort NxG Task Order. Under SOF AT&L, the Program Manager for Counterproliferation (PMCP) is chartered with the procurement, development, testing, training, fielding, and sustainment of technologies in support of Electronic Warfare (EW), advanced Counter Improvised Explosive Device (C-IED) operations and Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) for improvised explosive device threats and Counter-Unmanned System (C-UxS) threats. title: FSC Meridian Fire Reporting & Control Systems, NAS Meridian
description: Naval Air Station Meridian is located in east-central Mississippi, near Meridian, Mississippi in Lauderdale and Kemper counties. Approximately 20 miles northeast of the city of Meridian between State Highways 39 and 45. NAS Meridian hosts Training Air Wing One (TRAWING-1). The installation serves as a premier jet flight-training base, supporting Training Squadron 7 (VT-7) and Training Squadron 9 (VT-9). The air station trains hundreds of Navy and Marine Corps student aviators utilizing the T-45C Goshawk jet trainer. There are outlying fields used for student training. All maintenance and repair shall be performed by personnel trained and certified by the OEM. Personnel inspecting, witnessing tests, preparing reports, and issuing certificates for boilers and UPVs must be qualified per UFC 3-430-07. Personnel inspecting, certifying, and making recommendations for corrective action for backflow preventers shall be certified per UG-2029-ENV. Personnel working on fire protection systems must be certified per UFC 3-601-02 and shall be licensed in the state of Mississippi, as applicable. Fire Protection services shall be managed by a qualified individual who is NICET level III certified in fire alarm or NICET level III certified in special hazards systems. Personnel working on fire protection systems shall be certified in accordance with the requirements below: Fire Alarm Systems: ? Fire Alarm: NICET Level II certification in Fire Alarm Systems. ? Detection and releasing systems for Special Hazard Systems such as those found in aircraft hangars and computer server rooms: NICET Level II certification in Special Hazard Systems Water Based Suppression Systems: ? Wet Pipe and Dry Pipe Sprinklers: NICET Level II certification in Inspection and Testing of Water Based Systems. ? Pre-Action, Deluge, Foam and Antifreeze Systems: NICET Level III certification in Inspection and Testing of Water Based Systems. Special Hazard Systems: ? Clean Agent, CO2 and Combination Detection/Releasing Systems: NICET Level II certification in Special Hazard Systems. Pre-Engineered Kitchen Fire Extinguishing Systems: ? NICET Level II certification in Special Hazards Suppression Systems or certified by ICC/NAFED in Pre-Engineered Kitchen Fire Extinguishing Systems. The service technician shall have the applicable manufacturer�s design, installation, and maintenance manual and service bulletins. Less qualified personnel may assist NICET Levels II and III certified personnel in the execution of inspection, testing, maintenance and repair task. At no time shall less qualified personnel be allowed to execute inspection, testing, maintenance and repair task without a qualified NICET Level II or III. The Contractor shall also perform maintenance on NAS Meridian Water Plant SCADA system to ensure proper operation, to minimize breakdowns, and to maximize useful life.The Contractor shall conduct annual testing, calibration and adjustment of the system form the control point to the terminations at the monitoring devices, individual well houses, chemical mixers or injectors, valves and motor controllers. The performance of this contract requires maintenance, monitoring, programming, and integration services on specific proprietary control systems, Life Safety systems, and Industrial Control Systems (ICS). These include, but are not limited to, Johnson Controls, Simplex, Monaco, and Honeywell systems, as well as SCADA (Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition) water control systems. Interested sources must demonstrate existing technical competency, direct access to necessary proprietary software/firmware/tools, and current Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) authorization, certifications, or formal partnership agreements required to service, modify, and maintain these proprietary systems without voiding warranties or compromising system integrity. Respondents should be prepared to provide: (1) Proof of active OEM authorization/certification or licensed integrator status for the listed proprietary systems; (2) Evidence of personnel holding relevant manufacturer credentials/certifications (e.g., NICET II+ for fire alarm systems, certified ICS/PLC programmers for plant control); and (3) A brief summary of past performance involving identical or similar proprietary systems within an operational environment.

title: Access to Food and Cosmetic Product and Packaging Databases
description: The scope of this contract is to acquire the full range of technical, management and support services necessary to obtain and maintain access to US food and cosmetic products. The contract is divided into the following task areas: Project Management Data Access Data Collection Training Support 6.1 Technical Requirements 6.1.1 Datasets The processed food and cosmetic products and their package data (as well as menu data) shall be from a currently existing, commercially available database(s) that shall provide immediate automated access. The data shall include products from all regions of the US (Appendix B indicates the US Census regions) and be accurate, quality-assured, and easily-validated; well organized; stored as relationally searchable information for trend and other analyses; and fully exportable. The database(s) shall be regularly updated and maintained in a current state throughout the base and option periods. Information will be required for the following product types: Processed, and retail food products (e.g. foods, infant formula, etc.; minimum 400,000 products that are selling on the market in the contract year) and thus, over 2 million historical products; (Optional) Restaurant food products/menu items (minimum 50,000 products from top chains) Dietary supplements (minimum 100,000 products); shall be categorized according to the definition in Appendix A Cosmetics (minimum 300,000 products) The following attributes (as shown on the package) shall be required: Package images (legible images of all surfaces (e.g. sides, top, bottom) of product packaging, including internal and external packaging Count of available images per product Information contained on and in product packaging � shall include the following at minimum (each data entry line in the database must be quality assured and -controlled (QA/QC�d) for accuracy as the database is populated) GTIN/UPC/Barcode Nutrition Facts label, including single and dual columns and including multi-packs (shall be displayed in format according to 21 CFR 101.9) and Supplement Facts label (shall be displayed in format according to 21 CFR 101.36(e)(10) (i), (ii), (iii), and (iv)) Additional nutrients presenting on package labels Indication of added sugars Ingredients list (e.g. food additives, active ingredients for dietary supplements) Allergen labeling information (Contains/may contain) and advisory statements Pack size and weight Number of servings per package Brand Manufacturer Location of manufacturer, packer, or distributor Written and/or pictorial statements signaling the presence of one or more allergens (according to the Food Allergen Labeling and Consumer Protection Act (FALCPA) of 2004; title: Aircraft Rescue and Firefighting (ARFF) Fire Suppression Systems
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Offers are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number W913E526QA012 is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for Aircraft Rescue and Fire Fighting (ARFF) Fire Suppression Equipment. This acquisition is not set-aside for small business concerns. This solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses by reference. The full text of provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically at www.acquisition.gov. Contract Line Items CLIN 0001 � ARFF Fire Suppression Systems Quantity: 6 Each The Contractor shall provide six (6) complete ARFF fire suppression systems for integration into separately procured Antarctic ARFF vehicles in accordance with Section C, Description of Requirement (DOR). The systems shall include the required equipment, components, spare parts, non-standard tools, manuals, warranty, and product support specified in the DOR. CLIN 0002 � Initial Wet Firefighting Agent Quantity: 6 Each The Contractor shall provide the initial wet firefighting agent for each of the six (6) fire suppression systems, consisting of 400 gallons per system, in accordance with Section C, DOR. CLIN 0003 � Initial Dry Firefighting Agent Quantity: 6 Each The Contractor shall provide the initial dry firefighting agent for each of the six (6) fire suppression systems, consisting of 500 pounds per system, in accordance with Section C, DOR. CLIN 0004 � Nitrogen Gas Generator Quantity: 1 Each The Contractor shall provide one (1) nitrogen gas generator capable of supporting the nitrogen charging requirements specified in Section C, DOR. CLIN 0005 � Shipping and Handling Quantity: 1 Job The Contractor shall provide shipping and handling of Contractor-furnished equipment to the designated TBD CONUS integration contractor's facility in accordance with Section C, DOR. For quotation pricing purposes, the Government estimates a not-to-exceed (NTE) amount of $60,000 for shipping and handling. CLIN 0006 � Installation and Integration Support Quantity: 1 Job The Contractor shall provide installation and integration support for the ARFF fire suppression systems at the designated TBD CONUS integration contractor's facility in accordance with Section C, DOR. This effort includes the required system operability testing following installation and integration. CLIN 0007 � Integration Coordination and Engineering Support Quantity: 1 Job The Contractor shall provide coordination and engineering support necessary to facilitate successful integration of the fire suppression systems with the separately procured ARFF vehicles, including required technical information, drawings, and interface data, in accordance with Section C, DOR. CLIN 0008 � Training Quantity: 1 Job The Contractor shall provide required training to Government personnel at the designated TBD CONUS integration contractor's facility in accordance with Section C, DOR. CLIN 0009 � Contractor Travel Quantity: 1 Job The Contractor shall provide all Contractor travel required to support installation, integration, system operability testing, training, warranty, and product support in accordance with Section C, DOR. Description of Requirement The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Engineer Research and Development Center (ERDC), Cold Regions Research and Engineering Laboratory (CRREL), requires ARFF fire suppression equipment for integration into separately procured ARFF vehicles intended for operation in Antarctica. The requirement includes six (6) fire suppression systems providing both wet-agent and dry-chemical firefighting capability; one (1) nitrogen gas generator; initial quantities of required wet and dry firefighting agents; installation and integration support; integration coordination and engineering support; system operability testing; training; spare parts, non-standard tools, and manuals; warranty and product support; shipping and handling; and required Contractor travel. The Government will accept either a low-temperature compressed air foam system (CAFS) used in conjunction with a separate compatible dry-chemical system or another compatible wet-agent/dry-agent fire suppression system configuration that satisfies all requirements of Section C, DOR. The fire suppression equipment is intended for extreme cold-weather operations. The complete fire suppression system shall be fully operable at ambient temperatures down to -40�F with limited input from the heater installed in the truck body. The wet firefighting agent shall remain operational and suitable for use and storage at temperatures down to -40�F. The dry firefighting agent shall retain its required performance at temperatures down to -60�F. When properly configured for cold storage, the complete system shall withstand storage temperatures down to -60�F without damage or permanent loss of operability. No water shall be stored in or dispersed by the fire suppression equipment. The prime mover vehicles and associated vehicle bodies are being acquired separately and are not included in this acquisition. Delivery and Acceptance Contractor-furnished equipment shall be delivered to the TBD CONUS integration contractor's facility for installation and integration with the separately procured ARFF vehicles. The Quoter shall provide its estimated production completion and delivery schedule in accordance with Section C, DOR. The production and delivery schedule is required for Government planning and coordination. FOB: Destination. Inspection and acceptance shall be in accordance with the attached RFQ. Quoters are directed to the attached RFQ W913E526QA012, including Section C, Description of Requirement; Section L, Instructions to Quoters; and Section M, Evaluation Factors for Award, for the complete solicitation requirements, instructions, provisions, clauses, and terms and condition. Evaluation and Basis for Award Award will be made to the responsible Quoter whose quotation, conforming to the solicitation, represents the best value to the Government, price and other factors considered. The following factors will be used to evaluate quotations: Technical Capability Comparable Equipment Experience Price Technical Capability is more important than Comparable Equipment Experience. All evaluation factors other than Price, when combined, are significantly more important than Price. As quotations become more equal in their non-price merits, Price will become increasingly important in the award decision. Only technically acceptable quotations will be eligible for award. The Government may select a higher-priced technically acceptable quotation when meaningful advantages associated with Technical Capability and/or Comparable Equipment Experience warrant the additional price. The production and delivery schedule is required for Government planning and coordination and will not, by itself, be used as a discriminator among technically acceptable quotations. The detailed evaluation criteria and basis for award are contained in Section M of the attached RFQ. Quotation Submission Quotations are due no later than 12:00 PM Central Time on Friday, September 25, 2026. Quotations shall be submitted via email to: Kim D. Roberson Contract Specialist Email: Kim.D.Roberson@usace.army.mil Quoters shall comply with all quotation submission requirements contained in Section L of the attached RFQ, including submission of a signed and dated copy of the RFQ and acknowledgment of all amendments, if applicable. To be eligible for award, the Quoter shall maintain an active Federal Government contracts registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) when the quotation is submitted and at the time of award. Solicitation Provisions and Contract Clauses The solicitation provisions and contract clauses applicable to this acquisition are provided in the attached RFQ W913E526QA0

The work performed will be complex in nature, require multiple construction trades, and may require engineering design performed by credentialed professionals. Project execution methods will fall into one of the following classifications. The execution method will be defined in the project documents for each Task Order (TO) under this Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quanity (IDIQ) contract. Design Build will include the Contractor providing both the design and construction services for a project; during the Design-Build process, final design solutions are provided by the Contractor, not the Government. The Government will provide a Statement of Work (SOW), drawings, and other preliminary documents to establish requirements from the work to be completed. These documents will be equivalent to a schematic 15% or greater design. When awarded the TO for the project, the Contractor will complete the design to the 100% level to include drawings, specifications, design analysis/narrative, and other documentation as required by the Government. Construction with Limited Design method will include the Government providing the design and the Contractor will further develop portions as required and will provide construction services for the project. This method will be used for non-complex or repetitive work types of projects where design cost and effort is not warranted. The Government will provide the SOW, drawings, and other documents as necessary to establish requirements to complete the project. These documents will be equivalent to a design submittal 35% to 65%. When awarded the TO the Contractor will complete any additional design efforts required by the project and produce a set of working documents for use during construction. Construction only method will include the Government providing 100% design package, including the SOW, drawings, specification, and any other documents as necessary to establish requirements for the work to be accomplished. When awarded the TO the Contractor shall commence with construction in accordance with the design and contract requirements. The Contractor is required to furnish all materials, labor, plant, tools, transportation, equipment, testing services, quality control, and incidentals necessary to provide a complete useable end product as specified in the TO/project documents. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code is 236210, Industrial Building Construction with a small business size standard of $45 million. The MACC will be executed for one base period of five (5) years with one option period of five (5) years. The Government will negotiate equitable adjustments resulting from change orders in the shortest practicable time. Approximately 120 days are required to definitize equitable adjustments associated with change orders for construction. The definitization of an equitable adjustment begins when the contracting officer receives an adequate change order definitization proposal and ends when the contracting officer executes a contractual action to definitize the change order. The work performed will be complex in nature, require multiple construction trades, and may require engineering design performed by credentialed professionals. Project execution methods will fall into one of the following classifications. The execution method will be defined in the project documents for each Task Order (TO) under this Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quanity (IDIQ) contract. Design Build will include the Contractor providing both the design and construction services for a project; during the Design-Build process, final design solutions are provided by the Contractor, not the Government. The Government will provide a Statement of Work (SOW), drawings, and other preliminary documents to establish requirements from the work to be completed. These documents will be equivalent to a schematic 15% or greater design. When awarded the TO for the project, the Contractor will complete the design to the 100% level to include drawings, specifications, design analysis/narrative, and other documentation as required by the Government. Construction with Limited Design method will include the Government providing the design and the Contractor will further develop portions as required and will provide construction services for the project. This method will be used for non-complex or repetitive work types of projects where design cost and effort is not warranted. The Government will provide the SOW, drawings, and other documents as necessary to establish requirements to complete the project. These documents will be equivalent to a design submittal 35% to 65%. When awarded the TO the Contractor will complete any additional design efforts required by the project and produce a set of working documents for use during construction. Construction only method will include the Government providing 100% design package, including the SOW, drawings, specification, and any other documents as necessary to establish requirements for the work to be accomplished. When awarded the TO the Contractor shall commence with construction in accordance with the design and contract requirements. The Contractor is required to furnish all materials, labor, plant, tools, transportation, equipment, testing services, quality control, and incidentals necessary to provide a complete useable end product as specified in the TO/project documents. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code is 236210, Industrial Building Construction with a small business size standard of $45 million. The MACC will be executed for one base period of five (5) years with one option period of five (5) years. The Government will negotiate equitable adjustments resulting from change orders in the shortest practicable time. Approximately 120 days are required to definitize equitable adjustments associated with change orders for construction. The definitization of an equitable adjustment begins when the contracting officer receives an adequate change order definitization proposal and ends when the contracting officer executes a contractual action to definitize the change order. title: Notice Of Intent to Sole Source - Thermo Fisher Scientific Asheville LLC - Centrifuge Calibration
description: The purpose of this acquisition is to have Health Effects Laboratory Division (HELD) centrifuges undergo preventative maintenance and calibration. Regular calibration of centrifuges is essential because it ensures that rotational speed, temperature control (when applicable), and timing functions remain accurate, which directly affects the reliability and reproducibility of experimental results. The vendor shall perform visual and functional checks for rotor condition, imbalance indicators, lid locks, refrigeration performance (where applicable), and overall mechanical integrity. Key parameters will be calibrated according to International Standard Organization (ISO) 17025 standards.

title: Enterprise Data Pipeline Modernization and Data Consumption Services
description: Description: Enterprise Data Pipeline Modernization and Data Consumption Services Purpose and Disclaimer. The Internal Revenue Service (IRS) is issuing this Sources Sought Synopsis for market research purposes to identify capable sources and obtain industry information that will assist the Government in refining its acquisition strategy for Enterprise Data Pipeline Modernization and Data Consumption Services. The Government seeks information regarding commercial availability, capable sources, small business and socioeconomic capabilities, existing contract vehicles, customary commercial practices, and recommendations that may improve competition, performance outcomes, and acquisition efficiency. A Draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) is attached to this Sources Sought Notice and provides additional information regarding the Government's contemplated requirements. The Draft PWS is provided solely for market research and planning purposes and remains subject to change based on market research results and the Government's evolving requirements. There is no solicitation at this time. This notice is not a Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quotation (RFQ), Invitation for Bid, or commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or make an award. Responses are voluntary and will not be considered proposals. The Government will not reimburse respondents for costs incurred in preparing or submitting a response. Respondents should clearly mark proprietary information and should avoid submitting unnecessary proprietary or sensitive information. NAICS Code: 541512 - Computer Systems Design Services. PSC: DA01 - Business Application/application Development Support Services (labor) Background. The IRS is continuing modernization of its Individual Master File (IMF) Program and related taxpayer account processing and data management capabilities. Key initiatives include Individual Tax Processing Engine (ITPE)/Customer Account Data Engine (CADE) 2, Enterprise Data Platform (EDP), Taxpayer Account Management Services (TAMS), IMF Retirement Acceleration (IMFRA), implementation of legislative requirements, and Filing Season readiness. The contemplated requirement will provide enterprise data pipeline modernization, systems integration, technical engineering, data consumption, cybersecurity, DevSecOps, production support, and knowledge-transfer services to sustain and advance these modernization efforts. General Description of Work. The contemplated requirement includes enterprise data pipeline modernization; data engineering and integration; data product development and business intelligence consumption; metadata, governance, security, and data quality; self-service analytics and natural-language query enablement; AI-assisted legacy modernization support; DevSecOps and automation; testing and production readiness; operations and maintenance; and transition and knowledge-transfer services. See Attachment 1 - Draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) for the complete contemplated scope of work. Market Research Objectives. The Government will use information received to assess market capacity, commercial availability, potential acquisition vehicles, small business participation, teaming and subcontracting approaches, and other acquisition considerations. No decision regarding contract vehicle, competition approach, contract type, or set-aside status has been made. Capability Statement and Market Research Questions. Interested parties shall review the attached Draft PWS and provide a concise, tailored response addressing the following: Organization name, address, website, point of contact, telephone number, email address, Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), business size under NAICS 541512, and applicable socioeconomic status. Whether your organization can perform the full scope of the Draft PWS as a prime contractor. If not, identify the specific functional areas your organization can perform. Describe recent and relevant experience performing enterprise data pipeline modernization, data engineering, systems integration, data consumption, DevSecOps, cybersecurity, production support, and related services of comparable scope, scale, and complexity. Identify the customer, approximate value, period of performance, and relevance to this requirement. Describe the organizational, staffing, technical, and management capabilities necessary to perform the requirement, including the ability to recruit, retain, and manage personnel and mitigate performance and schedule risk. If significant subcontracting or teaming is anticipated, describe the contemplated administrative and management structure and the capabilities expected from team members. Are the services described in the Draft PWS available in the commercial marketplace? Identify relevant customary commercial practices, terms, service models, or other market practices the Government should consider. Identify any Draft PWS requirements that may unnecessarily restrict competition or create significant cost, schedule, technical, or performance risk, and recommend alternatives where appropriate. Identify any existing Government contract vehicles available to your organization that could support this requirement, including GSA contract numbers, NASA SEWP contract numbers, or other applicable Governmentwide Acquisition Contract (GWAC) vehicles. Identify your recommended contract type, acquisition approach, or other acquisition strategy considerations and briefly explain why the recommendation would improve competition, innovation, performance outcomes, or acquisition efficiency. Contemplated Dollar Value and Period of Performance. The anticipated total value is between $15 million and $20 million for a one-year base period plus two (2) 12-month option periods. This estimate is provided solely for market research purposes and is subject to change. Contemplated Place of Performance. The primary place of performance is anticipated to be the Contractor's facility. Performance may also be required, as directed by the Government, at IRS locations including Lanham, Maryland; Memphis, Tennessee; Austin, Texas; Dallas, Texas; and Ogden, Utah. Other IRS locations may be added based on future requirements. Submission Instructions. Interested parties that consider themselves qualified to perform the contemplated services are invited to submit a response to this Sources Sought Notice no later than Friday, September 25, 2026, at 2:00 PM Eastern Time. Responses shall be emailed to Jared Alexis at jared.j.alexis@irs.gov and Ebenezer Owusu at ebenezer.k.owusu@irs.gov. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted or acknowledged, and the Government does not intend to provide individual evaluations or feedback regarding capability submissions. Questions. Questions concerning this Sources Sought Notice should be submitted in writing to Contract Specialist Jared Alexis at jared.j.alexis@irs.gov. Attachment: Attachment 1 - Draft Performance Work Statement (PWS), Enterprise Data Pipeline Modernization and Data Consumption Services

description: This notice announces the intent by the Defense Health Agency Contracting Activity (DHACA) Fort Detrick, Maryland, 21702, to award a sole source Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Contract to Collaborative Testing Services (CTS) under the statutory authority 12.102(a). The contract is for the purchase of Scheduled proficiency tests shipped at specified dates (vendor dependent) to include testing materials (bloodstains, dried body fluid stains, dried saliva samples) for the Armed Forces Medical Examiner System (AFMES), Armed Forces DNA Identification Laboratory (AFDIL). Collaborative Testing Services, LLC (CTS) is the only responsible source capable of providing the highly specialized proficiency testing supplies and services required to maintain the accreditation and operational integrity of the Armed Forces DNA Identification Laboratory (AFMES/AFDIL). While four proficiency testing providers are recognized by laboratory accrediting bodies�Collaborative Testing Services, Bode Cellmark Forensics, College of American Pathologists (CAP), and Serological Research Institute (SERI)�comprehensive market research and technical evaluation confirm that only CTS satisfies the agency�s minimum operational, throughput, and scientific requirements. The remaining three providers present critical technical deficiencies that make them unsuitable for AFDIL�s casework requirements: Bode Cellmark Forensics offers infrequent testing schedules that cannot support AFDIL�s staffing capacity or rolling test intervals; SERI imposes compressed completion windows that are incompatible with the extended processing times required by AFDIL�s advanced testing technologies; and CAP utilizes a manual, scan-based submission process that introduces an unacceptable risk of data transcription errors. In contrast, CTS uniquely provides the validated test substrates, electronic reporting infrastructure, and staggered distribution schedules necessary to efficiently test personnel on a continuous basis without disrupting critical forensic operations. Procuring these tests from any other source would jeopardize compliance with time-sensitive accreditation standards, compromise the validity of future casework, and introduce substantial risks to the laboratory's mission. CTS is the sole provider that meets all required sample matrices, capacity requirements, and distribution intervals. The work performed will be complex in nature, require multiple construction trades, and may require engineering design performed by credentialed professionals. Project execution methods will fall into one of the following classifications. The execution method will be defined in the project documents for each Task Order (TO) under this Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quanity (IDIQ) contract. Design Build will include the Contractor providing both the design and construction services for a project; during the Design-Build process, final design solutions are provided by the Contractor, not the Government. The Government will provide a Statement of Work (SOW), drawings, and other preliminary documents to establish requirements from the work to be completed. These documents will be equivalent to a schematic 15% or greater design. When awarded the TO for the project, the Contractor will complete the design to the 100% level to include drawings, specifications, design analysis/narrative, and other documentation as required by the Government. Construction with Limited Design method will include the Government providing the design and the Contractor will further develop portions as required and will provide construction services for the project. This method will be used for non-complex or repetitive work types of projects where design cost and effort is not warranted. The Government will provide the SOW, drawings, and other documents as necessary to establish requirements to complete the project. These documents will be equivalent to a design submittal 35% to 65%. When awarded the TO the Contractor will complete any additional design efforts required by the project and produce a set of working documents for use during construction. Construction only method will include the Government providing 100% design package, including the SOW, drawings, specification, and any other documents as necessary to establish requirements for the work to be accomplished. When awarded the TO the Contractor shall commence with construction in accordance with the design and contract requirements. The Contractor is required to furnish all materials, labor, plant, tools, transportation, equipment, testing services, quality control, and incidentals necessary to provide a complete useable end product as specified in the TO/project documents. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code is 236210, Industrial Building Construction with a small business size standard of $45 million. The MACC will be executed for one base period of five (5) years with one option period of five (5) years. The Government will negotiate equitable adjustments resulting from change orders in the shortest practicable time. Approximately 120 days are required to definitize equitable adjustments associated with change orders for construction. The definitization of an equitable adjustment begins when the contracting officer receives an adequate change order definitization proposal and ends when the contracting officer executes a contractual action to definitize the change order. SAR imagery�s benefits remain helpful to the persistence of USNIC�s operational programs of earth surface observation in the poor weather or illumination conditions of the polar latitudes. Delivery beyond this period prohibits the USNIC from fulfilling an operational requirement to produce timely products and respond to tactical needs. **See attached documents for information being requested and further details**

title: P110 CAPE CANAVERAL RAILHEAD AND TRANSFER FACILITIES AT KENNEDY SPACE CENTER, FLORIDA
description: This is a request for information/market survey. This is not a request for proposal, request for quote, or an invitation for bid. There will be no solicitation, specification, or drawings available at this time. Naval Facilities Engineering System Command (NAVFAC) Southeast is soliciting comments from the public addressing the potential use of Project Labor Agreements (PLA) for the following construction project. The construction project involves constructing railroad trackage to connect and facilitate the transfer from commercial rail to the on-base processing facility at Cape Canaveral. Constructs a low-rise open air standing seam-metal roofed canopy on a reinforced shallow foundation with wide-flange beams and columns and continuous footings for a Submarine Launched Ballistic Missile Processing Facility (Motor Transfer Facility). Functions include receiving and shipping missile motors, components and Active Inert Missiles (AIMS) which require superflat floors for air pallet operations. The roof structure will include sloped, uninsulated metal roof panels on steel joists. Project will be design-bid-build. NAICS Code: 237990. The magnitude of construction is anticipated to be $25,000,000 � $100,000,000. General period of performance is anticipated to be approximately 527 calendar days. A PLA is defined as a pre-hire collective bargaining agreement with one or more labor organizations that establishes the terms and conditions of employment for a specific construction project and is an agreement as described in 29 U.S.C. 158 (f). Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) policy states: Executive Order (E.O.) 14063, Use of Project Labor Agreements for Federal Construction Projects, requires agencies to use PLAs in large-scale construction projects (defined as a construction projects with a total estimated cost at or above $35M) to promote economy and efficiency in the administration and completion of Federal construction projects. When awarding a contract in connection with a large-scale construction project, agencies shall require use of a PLA for contractors and subcontractors engaged in construction on the project, unless an exception(s) at FAR 22.504(d) applies. Reference is made to: FAR Subpart 22.5 Use of Project Labor Agreements for Federal Construction Projects; provision, FAR 52.222-33 Notice of Requirement for Project Labor Agreement; and to clause, FAR 52.222-34 Project Labor Agreement. In consideration of the above factors, and any others which may be deemed appropriate, the public is invited to provide responses on the use of a PLA for this construction project utilizing the attached questionnaire. In light of recent court decisions on PLAs, the Government is seeking additional information on the use of PLAs for this project. This survey is for planning purposes only and shall not be construed as an obligation on the part of the Government. The Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of this market survey or otherwise pay for the requested information. The Government will not provide a debriefing on the results of this survey. All information will be held in a confidential manner and will only be used for the purposes intended. (See question #4) Responses shall be submitted on the attached questionnaire via email to Deborah Torrence, deborah.d.torrence2.civ@us.navy.mil no later than 2:00 PM ET on September 25, 2026.

title: Blanket Purchase Agreement - Sample Testing
description: The requirement is for the establishment of single Blanket Purchase Agreements (BPA) for the testing of metal coupons to aid the QA process of the components with which these coupons are associated. The Contractor�s laboratory facility must be validated by the USACE Materials Testing Center (MTC) along with maintain ISO/IEC 17025 certification and remain validated throughout the life of this agreement. Project Background The Contractor shall receive, test mechanical and/or chemical characteristics, and submit reports of coupon materials to aid the QA process of the associated components supplied to the Government via other ongoing contract efforts. The coupons will be shipped directly to the Contractor, many of which will likely come from international locations. The Contractor will not be responsible for shipping or duty costs to receive coupons. The coupon materials that may be tested include but may not be limited to ASTM A743 Grade CA6NM and Grade CF3, ASTM A27 Grade 70-40, ASTM A148 Grade 80-40, ASTM A216 Grade WCC, and ASTM A516 Grade 60. The tests that may be required include chemical analysis according to ASTM A751, carbon combustion according to ASTM E1019-18, tensile tests (yield strength, tensile strength, elongation, and reduction of area) according to ASTM A370, hardness tests according to ASTM A370, and Charpy v-notch impact tests according to ASTM A370. The range of tests completed for a given coupon will depend on the material and component with which it is associated. There may be provisions for optional storage of coupons, both tested and untested. Disposal of excess coupons may be considered at no additional cost to the Government.

title: BEYOND Phase 2
description: Amendment 0001 is hereby issued to extend the proposal due date of the SIR to September 25, 2026 at 3:00pm ET. No other changes result from Amendment 0001. __________________________________________________ This is the Screening Information Request (SIR) 697DCK-26-R-00423 for the BEYOND Phase 2 Selection. This procurement is in support of the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), Unmanned Aircraft Systems and Advanced Air Mobility Integration Office (AUS). The FAA Reauthorization Act of 2024 (P.L.118-63) Section 920 allows for the expansion of the BEYOND program. The FAA will implement a BEYOND Phase 2 competitive selection process, through this SIR. This competitive selection process is not a procurement or acquisition under the FAA Acquisition Management System. The FAA did not develop any acquisition requirements for this competitive selection process, and the process will not result in the award of a procurement contract. Consistent with the FAA Administrator�s authorities under 49 U.S.C. �106(l) and (m), this process will result in the award of an Other Transaction Agreement (OTA). The FAA intends to award up to eight (8) OTAs through this solicitation. BEYOND Phase 2 has four programmatic focus areas: infrastructure, scalability, safety and automation. Five operational focus areas have also been identified as the greatest challenges that will need to be addressed for progress to be made: public safety, controlled airspace, remote, rural areas with inadequate infrastructure, on-airport operations and cross international borders. This SIR is seeking Offerors who can deliver successful outcomesin support of the BEYOND Phase 2 focus areas. See SIR for details. The FAA intends to competitively award up to eight (8) Other Transaction Agreements (OTAs) with SLTTs in accordance with the SIR. The FAA reserves the right to execute additional OTAs if resources permit (49 U.S.C. � 106(l)). The Government will make OTA awards to the Offeror�s determined to best meet the selection criteria which are included in this SIR and reflected in the evaluation of the proposals. To be considered for award of this requirement, the Offeror must have a current/valid registration in the Systems for Award Management (SAM) database website: www.sam.gov. Registration must be active by the offer due date. Proposals must be submitted via email to the Contracting Officer and Contract Specialist no later than 3:00 pm ET on September 10, 2026. Please see attached SIR for proposal submission requirements. Questions are to be submitted, in writing, as specified in the SIR. Please reference the SIR number and BEYOND Phase 2 program on all question submissions. All questions must be received no later than 1:00pm ET on September 3, 2026. Questions will be answered in an Amendment to the SIR if deemed necessary and posted to SAM.GOV for all interested parties to consider. Prospective Offerors are encouraged to frequently visit SAM.GOV for any updates to this requirement. Any questions regarding this announcement should be directed to Kristin Frantz, Contracting Officer, at Kristin.T.Frantz@faa.gov and Jackson LeMay, Contract Specialist, at Jackson.T.Lemay@faa.gov Any proposals received after the closing date and time, will not be considered in accordance with this SIR. This SIR is not to be construed as a contract or a commitment of any kind. The Government will not be liable for payment of any costs attributed to the preparation and submission of requested proposal documentation.
